newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JONES SETS SIGHTS ON NUMBER ONE RANKING.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JONES SETS SIGHTS ON NUMBER ONE RANKING.

text.p: Marion Jones, sprint queen of the sixth world championships, now has visions of becoming the world's top women's sprinter this season.

"I definitely want to be ranked number one in the world in both the 100 and 200 this year," said the world championships' only double winner after victories in the women's 100 metres and the 4x100 metres relay.
"I still want to run 10.7 for the 100 and sub-22 in the 200 this year," added the 21-year-old Jones, who returned to athletics this season after four years of college basketball.

"Everytime I run with Gail (Olympic champion Devers) in the 100 we have had some incredible performances, so I know in the next couple of weeks she will definitely put the pressure on me to run fast, and vice versa."
Jones also hopes to be the Grand Prix champion in the 200 metres. She did not qualify for the American team here but subsequently ran the season's fastest time of 22.16 seconds at Stockholm.
"I've got five big meets in the next two weeks," said Jones.
The whirlwind tour begins Wednesday in Zurich where she will contest both the 100 and 200 metres at the lucrative Weltklasse meeting.
"She is doubling up because she needs the grand prix points," said her manager, Charlie Wells.
Jones will also seek 200 metres victories in Monte Carlo and Cologne and race over 100 metres at Brussels and Berlin to complete her European season.
A 100 metres at Tokyo and the Grand Prix 200 metres final at Fukuoka, Japan, will conclude her year.
Her only disappointment so far has been the world championships' long jump where she placed 10th.
"I have so much potential," she said. "I haven't scratched the surface."
Help may be on the way.
"Jackie (former Olympic champion Jackie Joyner-Kersee) said she would love to come out to North Carolina and show me some technique," Jones said. "I was like, 'Please, please, please'.'"
" Overall there has never been anything in my life like this. It's one of those things I will definitely cherish, and if everything goes right, it will not be my last."
